# Adjudication Task — Chapter 463

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃463화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|희미한 빛이 스며드는 깊고 어두운 동굴 안. 자그마한 체구의 노인은 가부좌를 튼 채 자신을 관조하고 있었다.
  6|
  7|태양과도 같은 기운이 수백 개의 혈도를 지나 기경팔맥(奇經八脈)으로 치닫자, 유형의 기운이 일어나 노인의 전신을 감싸 안았다.
  8|
  9|그리고 이내 변화가 시작되었다.
 10|
 11|솨아아아.
 12|
 13|하얗게 센 노인의 머리 위로 세 개의 꽃봉오리가 피어오르고, 이내 사라졌다.
 14|
 15|꽃봉오리를 이룸과 동시에 흩어진 기운은 새로운 형상을 만들어냈다. 오색찬란한 빛을 띤 다섯 개의 원.
 16|
 17|초절정 고수 중에서도 선택받은 소수만이 이룩한 경지. 바로 오기조원(五氣朝元)에 다다른 자만이 보일 수 있는 현상이었다.
 18|
 19|하지만 노인을 둘러싼 변화는 그것으로 끝나지 않았다.
 20|
 21|화륵. 츠츠츠츠!
 22|
 23|오기조원을 상징하는 다섯 개의 원이 붉게 물들었다. 극강의 열양지기를 머금은 공력의 고리로부터 뿜어져 나온 엄청난 화기가 노인을 휘감고, 이내 푸른 빛을 띠었다.
 24|
 25|노화순청(爐火純靑).
 26|
 27|화로의 불이 뜨거워지면 푸른색으로 변하는 법. 노인이 이룩한 무공의 경지 역시 마찬가지였다.
 28|
 29|장장 백 년이 넘는 세월 동안 쌓이고 쌓인 공력과 깨달음은 이미 극의(極意)에 달했다고 해도 과언이 아니었다.
 30|
 31|그러나…….
 32|
 33|‘여기까지인가.’
 34|
 35|노인, 화왕(火王) 적천강은 공력을 거둬들였다. 가부좌를 튼 채 허공에 떠올라 있던 신형이 지면에 닿는 순간, 그를 둘러싼 기이한 현상도 씻은 듯이 사라졌다.
 36|
 37|고요한 공간에 남은 것은 적천강의 실소뿐이었다.
 38|
 39|“허허.”
 40|
 41|어찌하여 눈앞의 벽을 넘어 더 나아갈 수 없는가.
 42|
 43|그 사실을 누구보다 잘 알고 있기에 고개를 끄덕이면서도, 미동도 하지 않는 벽이 아쉽고 애석했다. 하늘이 원망스럽기도 했다.
 44|
 45|그러나 적천강은 미간을 찌푸리는 대신 웃음으로 씁쓸한 마음을 달랬다.
 46|
 47|‘무얼 원망할까. 노부가 자초한 일인 것을.’
 48|
 49|무공은 끊임없는 단련으로 강해지고, 깨달음은 마음을 비웠을 때 비로소 찾아온다.
 50|
 51|그러나 적천강은 지난 수십 년간 마음에 쌓인 찌꺼기를 비워 내지 못했다.
 52|
 53|이렇게 쌓이고 고인 것은 언젠가 썩는 법. 썩은 마음에 번뇌가 가득하니 심마(心魔)가 찾아왔고, 심마가 찾아오니 노환을 막을 수 없었다.
 54|
 55|“그나마 녀석을 만나지 않았다면…… 아마 지금쯤 벽에 똥칠하고 있었겠지. 허허.”
 56|
 57|적천강은 너털웃음을 지었다.
 58|
 59|한 번. 단 한 번의 작은 깨달음을 얻는다면 반로환동(返老還童)의 경지에 도달할 수 있을 것이다.
 60|
 61|하지만 그는 알고 있었다. 이 또한 욕심이라는 것을. 완전히 비우지 못한 마음이라는 것을.
 62|
 63|문득 고개를 들자 자그마한 구멍 사이로 하늘이 비친다. 적천강은 저 너머, 보이지 않는 누군가에게 물었다.
 64|
 65|“이것으로 만족하라는 뜻이구려. 맞소?”
 66|
 67|대답은 돌아오지 않았다. 아니, 어쩌면 이미 대답을 들었는지도 몰랐다.
 68|
 69|타고난 살귀(殺鬼)를 제자로 거두어 죄 없는 이들을 죽게 했으나, 두 번째 제자 덕분에 정신이라도 온전히 보전할 수 있게 되었으니 더 이상 어떤 미련도 갖지 말라는 대답.
 70|
 71|대답하는 존재는 없었지만, 적천강은 자신의 마음에서 들려오는 대답을 들었다.
 72|
 73|“참으로 지랄 같군. 노부가 지금껏 처리해 준 마두(魔頭)가 몇 놈인데 이런 푸대접이라니.”
 74|
 75|푸념 섞인 한숨을 내쉰 적천강이 고개를 내리며 말을 이었다.
 76|
 77|“그렇게 생각하지 않느냐?”
 78|
 79|적천강의 시선 끝에 선 한 사람, 와룡객(臥龍客) 제갈풍이 쥘부채를 흔들며 대답했다.
 80|
 81|“언젠가 조부께서 아홉 살이 된 저를 곁에 앉혀 두고 그런 말씀을 하셨지요. 저 위에 어떤 놈이 있는지는 몰라도, 참으로 지랄 같은 성미를 지닌 것이 분명하다. 지금 노 선배께서도 같은 말씀을 하시는군요.”
 82|
 83|적천강이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 84|
 85|“제갈공후, 그놈이 그래도 가끔가다 한 번씩 맞는 말을 하긴 했지.”
 86|
 87|“현명하신 분이었습니다.”
 88|
 89|“물론 네놈보다 똑똑하기도 했다. 적어도 조부뻘 되는 사람 앞에서 버르장머리 없게 부채질하진 않았으니. 그 부채 부숴 버리기 전에 당장 접어라.”
 90|
 91|“쉽게 부서질 만한 물건이 아닙니다. 만년한철을 두 냥이나 넣었거든요.”
 92|
 93|“네놈 골통도 만년한철이냐?”
 94|
 95|“아, 그렇군요. 가르침 감사합니다.”
 96|
 97|냉큼 부채를 접은 제갈풍이 동굴을 둘러보며 입을 열었다.
 98|
 99|“한데 이곳에는 어인 일로 오셨습니까? 이미 수색도 끝나 아무도 찾지 않는 곳인데.”
100|
101|“그러니 온 것이다. 노부야 기관진식에는 문외한이니, 나름대로 준비를 해야지.”
102|
103|준비라는 말에 제갈풍의 눈썹이 슬쩍 올라갔다.
104|
105|“전투가 벌어질 거라 생각하시는군요.”
106|
107|“항상 싸움을 대비하는 것이 무인의 자세. 더군다나 암천이라는 놈들은 잔학무도하고 집요하다. 이 정도로는 끝나지 않아.”
108|
109|적천강의 목소리는 무거웠다.
110|
111|암천에 의해 법왕 굉도라는 절친했던 벗을 잃은 그다.
112|
113|하남과 사천의 혈사가 낳은 수많은 죽음은 과거 일어났던 정마대전을 떠올리기에 충분했다.
114|
115|“사천당문의 지하 뇌옥에 천력마(天力魔)가 갇혀 있었다는 이야기는 알고 있으리라 생각한다.”
116|
117|“물론입니다. 그가 진 소협을 통해 암천을 마교의 후신(後身)이라 칭하고 죽음을 맞이했다는 것 역시.”
118|
119|천하의 패권을 두고 벌어진 정마대전은 정파의 승리로 막을 내렸지만, 그것은 대승이 아니라 상처뿐인 승리였다.
120|
121|만약 당시의 정파에 충분한 여력이 남았다면 퇴각하는 마교의 군세를 추격하여 모든 뿌리를 뽑았을 것이다.
122|
123|하지만 천마신교와 정파. 두 용과 호랑이는 종전과 동시에 대부분의 힘을 잃었고, 오십여 년이라는 긴 공백의 시간은 도망친 패자가 다시 일어나기에 충분한 시간이었다.
124|
125|암천(暗天)이라는 새로운 이름으로.
126|
127|“어느덧 세월이 이렇게 흘렀구나. 돌고 돌아 또다시 난세가 찾아오고 말았어.”
128|
129|적천강의 나직한 목소리에 제갈풍은 문득 고개를 들었다.
130|
131|천장의 틈 사이로 보이는 하늘은 어둡고 혼란했다. 당장 내일 저 먹구름이 사라지고 하늘이 푸르게 걷힌다 해도, 흐트러진 천기는 천하의 그 어떤 복자(卜者)도 읽어 낼 수 없을 것이다.
132|
133|‘난세.’
134|
135|바야흐로 돌고 돌아 찾아온 난세였고, 환란의 시대는 눈앞까지 들이닥쳤다.
136|
137|피가 강을 이루고 시체가 산처럼 쌓일 것이다.
138|
139|죽음과 파괴가 곳곳에서 자행되니 부모 잃은 고아가 천하를 떠돌 것이며, 썩어 가는 시신을 처리하지 못해 역병이 창궐하고 기근이 들 것이다.
140|
141|‘지금 벌어지는 일은 그 일부분에 불과하다.’
142|
143|그 사실을 다시 한번 깨달은 제갈풍은 오싹 소름이 돋았다. 하지만 그것은 비단 암천의 존재 때문만은 아니었다.
144|
145|“선객이 있었군.”
146|
147|귓가를 파고드는 누군가의 목소리. 제갈풍은 창졸간에 얼음물을 뒤집어쓴 사람처럼 우뚝 굳어 버렸다.
148|
149|‘어떻게?’
150|
151|비록 초절정의 경지에 이르지는 못했으나 제갈풍 역시 절정의 끝자락에 다다른 고수.
152|
153|그런 그가 어떤 기척도 느끼지 못했다. 소리도 들을 수 없었다.
154|
155|언제나 그림자처럼 따라다니는 호위 셋을 동굴 앞에 세워 두고 왔음에도 아무런 징조를 느끼지 못했다는 것은, 목소리의 주인이 최소 초절정의 고수라는 뜻이다.
156|
157|‘그 정도의 고수라면…….’
158|
159|마주 보고 있는 적천강을 제외하면 무당파의 현공진인 뿐.
160|
161|하지만 들려오는 목소리는 턱없이 젊고 맑았다. 마치 소년의 그것처럼.
162|
163|‘아.’
164|
165|제갈풍은 섬전 같은 깨달음과 함께 돌아섰다.
166|
167|몇 번인가 스치듯이 마주했던 소년 의생을 마주한 순간, 머릿속에 가득했던 안개가 흩어지고 한 사람의 별호가 입술 사이로 흘러나왔다.
168|
169|“살성(殺星).”
170|
171|소년 의생, 문경의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.
172|
173|“이미 알고 있었나?”
174|
175|“몰랐습니다. 방금까지는.”
176|
177|제갈풍은 흥분한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
178|
179|“하지만 고금제일의 살수가 사라진 이유에 대해서는 늘 의문이 남았지요. 어찌하여 신의라는 걸출한 의생이 정마대전이 끝난 후에야 등장했는가에 대해서도.”
180|
181|“제법이군.”
182|
183|“유심히 지켜본 적도 있었습니다만, 설마하니 반로환동의 경지에 드셨을 줄은 몰랐습니다.”
184|
185|살성은 알려진 바가 거의 없는 미지의 인물.
186|
187|번쩍이는 눈동자로 문경을 바라보던 제갈풍이 문득 멈칫했다.
188|
189|“한데 어째서 굳이 제게…… 혹시?”
190|
191|“눈치도 빠르고. 제갈가의 핏줄다워.”
192|
193|“아무래도 피는 못 속이는 법이지. 약간 이상한 것 같긴 해도 똘똘한 놈이야. 제갈공후가 손주 놈을 잘 키운 게야. 자, 그건 그렇고…….”
194|
195|어깨를 으쓱한 적천강이 문경을 응시하며 말을 이었다.
196|
197|“무슨 일인가? 어울리지도 않게 어린애 흉내나 내던 늙은이가 이리 다급하게 찾아온 연유가.”
198|
199|“짧게 말하지. 지금 당장 이곳을 떠나야 한다.”
200|
201|“뭐라?”
202|
203|문경이 말했듯이, 그의 말은 너무나도 짧았다.
204|
205|그리고 그것은 적천강에게 있어 저 빌어먹을 천령폭을 넘을만한 이유가 되기에는 턱없이 부족했다.
206|
207|“그게 무슨 개소리…….”
208|
209|“더 짧게 말해 줄 필요가 있겠군.”
210|
211|문경이 깊게 가라앉은 목소리로 말을 이었다.
212|
213|“네 제자가 위험하다. 아니, 어쩌면 모두가.”
214|
215|“……!”
216|
217|그 말을 들은 순간, 적천강은 더 이상의 어떤 이유도 필요하지 않음을 깨달았다.
218|
219|고개를 돌려 제갈풍을 바라보는 그의 노회한 눈동자에는, 어느새 푸른 불꽃이 깃들어 있었다.
220|
221|“배를 띄워라. 지금 당장.”
222|
223|
224|
225|* * *
226|
227|
228|
229|마지막 장소에 도착했을 무렵, 동정호의 강물은 자줏빛으로 물들어 있었다.
230|
231|절벽과 기암괴석(奇巖怪石)의 틈새로 비추는 석양을 바라본 내가 입을 열었다.
232|
233|“지금부터 함부로 움직이지 마. 나룻배는 안전한 곳에 묶어 두고, 땅으로 이동해서 만약의 사태를 대비해.”
234|
235|동정호는 호수지만 그 크기는 호수라고 부를 수 없을 만큼 광활하다.
236|
237|사방에 물만 있는 것이 아니라 작은 섬, 혹은 장강의 지류에서 흘러들어온 흙과 모래가 쌓여 축적된 평평한 지면도 어렵지 않게 볼 수 있었다.
238|
239|‘만약 전투가 시작된다면, 육지 위에서 싸우는 것이 훨씬 유리하다.’
240|
241|이중 수공을 익힌 사람은 아무도 없다.
242|
243|그나마 내가 [수상 구조대원]의 칭호 효과로 수중에서도 자유롭게 이동할 수 있긴 하지만, 무공의 위력이 20%나 감소하는 디버프를 피할 수는 없었다.
244|
245|‘만약 상황이 안 좋게 흘러간다면…… 최소한 육지에서 대응할 수 있어야 해.’
246|
247|이런 내 생각을 모를 리 없는 녀석들이다.
248|
249|궁기방이 결연한 표정으로 입을 열었다.
250|
251|“함께 가지.”
252|

“Blood will tell, after all. He may be a little strange, but the boy is clever. Zhuge Gonghu raised his grandson well. Now, putting that aside…”

[P103]
Jeok Cheongang shrugged and fixed his gaze on Mungyeong.

[P104]
“What brings you here? Why has an old man who’s been playing at being a child, despite it not suiting him in the slightest, come rushing over?”

[P105]
“I’ll keep it short. We must leave this place immediately.”

[P106]
“What?”

[P107]
As promised, Mungyeong’s answer was extremely brief.

[P108]
And for Jeok Cheongang, it was nowhere near reason enough to brave that godforsaken Tianling Falls.

[P109]
“What kind of bullshit is—”

[P110]
“I should make it even shorter.”

[P111]
Mungyeong continued in a low, grave voice.

[P112]
“Your disciple is in danger. No—perhaps everyone is.”

[P113]
“……!”

[P114]
The moment he heard those words, Jeok Cheongang realized he needed no further explanation.

[P115]
He turned toward Zhuge Feng. Blue flames had already kindled in his aged eyes.

[P116]
“Launch the boat. Right now.”

[P117]
* * *

[P118]
By the time we reached the final location, the waters of Dongting Lake had turned purple.

[P119]
I gazed at the sunset shining through the gaps between the cliffs and jagged rock formations, then spoke.

[P120]
“Don’t move around carelessly from here on. Tie the ferryboat somewhere safe, get onto land, and prepare for anything.”

[P121]
Dongting Lake was called a lake, but it was so vast that the name hardly seemed adequate.

[P122]
There wasn’t water in every direction. Small islands were easy enough to find, as were flat stretches of land formed by mud and sand carried in from tributaries of the Yangtze.

[P123]
*If a battle breaks out, fighting on land will put us at a much greater advantage.*

[P124]
None of us had mastered water arts.

[P125]
I could at least move freely underwater thanks to the Water Rescue Worker Title, but even I could not avoid the debuff that reduced the power of my martial arts by twenty percent.

[P126]
*If things go badly… we need to be able to fight back on land, at the very least.*

[P127]
The others understood my reasoning perfectly well.

[P128]
Gung Gibang spoke with a determined expression.

[P129]
“I’ll go with you.”

[P130]
“Can you swim?”

[P131]
“I can dog-paddle a little.”

[P132]
“Get onto land before I beat you like a dog.”

[P133]
“Hmm. That would probably be better.”

[P134]
Gung Gibang stepped back, and Hyuk Mujin came forward.

[P135]
“Captain.”

[P136]
“You stay on land too. Keep your head down and hide. You won’t be any help if you charge in for no reason.”

[P137]
“I know. I only called out to encourage you.”

[P138]
“……”

[P139]
What a sibu-leol bastard. I felt what little strength I had left draining away.

[P140]
I let out a small sigh, then gave Cheongpung one final, earnest warning.

[P141]
“The Dongting Fisherman may or may not be in there. But if I find him and drag him outside…”

[P142]
Cheongpung nodded.

[P143]
“I won’t miss the opportunity.”

[P144]
“Good. That’s all I need.”

[P145]
I had no idea just how formidable the Dongting Fisherman was, but with Cheongpung’s help, things would be much easier.

[P146]
*Of course, he might not be here either.*

[P147]
But… how should I put it?

[P148]
This time felt different.

[P149]
It wasn’t reason. It was instinct.

[P150]
I looked at each of them in turn, then leaped without hesitation into the purple water.

[P151]
*Splash!*

[P152]
The familiar sensation washed over me as a System notification rang out.

[P153]
The Title’s effect activated. Transparent webbing formed between my fingers and toes, and breathing became easy.

[P154]
*Deeper. Farther in.*

[P155]
I pressed onward without stopping.

[P156]
I swam swiftly through the cold water, passing countless fish.

[P157]
Then I spotted something in the distance.

[P158]
*What’s that…?*

[P159]
Far ahead, a pitch-black cave came into view.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“He was also smarter than you. At least he didn’t have the bad manners to wave a fan in front of someone old enough to be his grandfather. Fold that thing before I break it.”

[P47]
“It will not break easily. I had two nyang of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron worked into it.”

[P48]
“Is your skull made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron too?”

[P49]
“Ah, I see. Thank you for the lesson.”

[P50]
Zhuge Feng promptly folded his fan, then looked around the cave.

[P51]
“But what brings you here? The search is already over, and no one comes here anymore.”

[P52]
“That is precisely why I came. This old man knows nothing about mechanisms and formations, so I have to prepare in my own way.”

[P53]
At the word *prepare*, Zhuge Feng’s eyebrows rose slightly.

[P54]
“You believe there will be a battle.”

[P55]
“A martial artist should always be prepared for a fight. Besides, those Dark Heaven bastards are brutal and persistent. This will not end here.”

[P56]
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was heavy.

[P57]
Dark Heaven had taken the life of his close friend, Dharma King Hong Dao.

[P58]
The countless deaths caused by the bloodshed in Henan and Sichuan were more than enough to remind him of the Great Faction War.

[P59]
“I assume you know that the Heavenly Power Demon was imprisoned in the underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P60]
“Of course. I also know that before his death, he told Young Hero Jin that Dark Heaven was the successor to the Demonic Cult.”

[P61]
The Great Faction War, fought for supremacy over the world, had ended in victory for the orthodox faction. But it had not been a sweeping victory. It was a victory that left nothing but wounds.

[P62]
Had the orthodox faction retained enough strength at the time, it would have pursued the retreating forces of the Demonic Cult and torn out every last root.

[P63]
But the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult and the orthodox faction—the dragon and tiger—had both lost most of their strength when the war ended. The long interval of more than fifty years had given the defeated survivors ample time to rise again.

[P64]
Under a new name.

[P65]
Dark Heaven.

[P66]
“So much time has passed before we knew it. The wheel has turned, and troubled times have come again.”

[P67]
At Jeok Cheongang’s quiet words, Zhuge Feng looked up.

[P68]
The sky visible through the cracks in the cave ceiling was dark and chaotic. Even if the black clouds vanished tomorrow and the blue sky emerged, the heavenly patterns had already fallen into such disarray that no diviner in the world could read them.

[P69]
*Troubled times.*

[P70]
After completing its long circle, an age of turmoil had returned. An era of calamity was already upon them.

[P71]
Blood would flow in rivers, and corpses would pile up like mountains.

[P72]
Death and destruction would run rampant. Orphans who had lost their parents would wander the world, while plague and famine spread because there would be no one to dispose of the rotting bodies.

[P73]
*What is happening now is only a small part of it.*

[P74]
As Zhuge Feng realized that once more, a chill ran down his spine.

[P75]
But Dark Heaven was not the only reason.

[P76]
“I see you already had a guest.”

[P77]
A voice pierced his ears.

[P78]
Zhuge Feng froze as though someone had dumped ice water over his head.

[P79]
*How?*

[P80]
Though he had not reached the Supreme Peak realm, Zhuge Feng was still a master standing at the very edge of Peak.

[P81]
Yet he had sensed no presence. Heard no sound.

[P82]
He had left three guards who followed him like shadows outside the cave, but none of them had given the slightest warning. That meant the owner of the voice was at least a Supreme Peak master.

[P83]
*If he’s that powerful…*

[P84]
Aside from Jeok Cheongang, the only possibility was Perfected Being Hyeongong of Wudang.

[P85]
But the voice was far too young and clear.

[P86]
It sounded like a boy’s.

[P87]
*Ah.*

[P88]
Insight flashed through Zhuge Feng’s mind, and he spun around.

[P89]
The moment he saw the young medical apprentice he had encountered several times in passing, the fog in his mind dispersed, and a sobriquet slipped from his lips.

[P90]
“The Slaughter Saint.”

[P91]
Mungyeong’s eyebrow twitched.

[P92]
“You already knew?”

[P93]
“I did not. Not until just now.”

[P94]
Zhuge Feng continued excitedly.

[P95]
“But I have always wondered why the greatest assassin in history disappeared. I also wondered why an extraordinary healer known as the Divine Physician appeared only after the Great Faction War had ended.”

[P96]
“Not bad.”

[P97]
“I watched you closely once, but I never imagined that you had reached the realm of Returned to Youth.”

[P98]
Almost nothing was known about the Slaughter Saint. He was a figure shrouded in mystery.

[P99]
Zhuge Feng stared at Mungyeong with gleaming eyes, then suddenly hesitated.

[P100]
“But why would you deliberately reveal yourself to me… Unless?”

[P101]
“You’re quick. Worthy of the Zhuge bloodline.”

[P102]
“Blood will tell, after all. He may be a little strange, but the boy is clever. Zhuge Gonghu raised his grandson well. Now, putting that aside…”

[P103]
Jeok Cheongang shrugged and fixed his gaze on Mungyeong.

[P104]
“What brings you here? Why has an old man who’s been playing at being a child, despite it not suiting him in the slightest, come rushing over?”

[P105]
“I’ll keep it short. We must leave this place immediately.”

[P106]
“What?”

[P107]
As promised, Mungyeong’s answer was extremely brief.

[P108]
And for Jeok Cheongang, it was nowhere near reason enough to brave that godforsaken Tianling Falls.

[P109]
“What kind of bullshit is—”

[P110]
“I should make it even shorter.”

[P111]
Mungyeong continued in a low, grave voice.

[P112]
“Your disciple is in danger. No—perhaps everyone is.”

[P113]
“……!”

[P114]
The moment he heard those words, Jeok Cheongang realized he needed no further explanation.

[P115]
He turned toward Zhuge Feng. Blue flames had already kindled in his aged eyes.

[P116]
“Launch the boat. Right now.”

[P117]
* * *

[P118]
By the time we reached the final location, the waters of Dongting Lake had turned purple.

[P119]
I gazed at the sunset shining through the gaps between the cliffs and jagged rock formations, then spoke.

[P120]
“Don’t move around carelessly from here on. Tie the ferryboat somewhere safe, get onto land, and prepare for anything.”

[P121]
Dongting Lake was called a lake, but it was so vast that the name hardly seemed adequate.

[P122]
There wasn’t water in every direction. Small islands were easy enough to find, as were flat stretches of land formed by mud and sand carried in from tributaries of the Yangtze.

[P123]
*If a battle breaks out, fighting on land will put us at a much greater advantage.*

[P124]
None of us had mastered water arts.

[P125]
I could at least move freely underwater thanks to the Water Rescue Worker Title, but even I could not avoid the debuff that reduced the power of my martial arts by twenty percent.

[P126]
*If things go badly… we need to be able to fight back on land, at the very least.*

[P127]
The others understood my reasoning perfectly well.

[P128]
Gung Gibang spoke with a determined expression.

[P129]
“I’ll go with you.”

[P130]
“Can you swim?”

[P131]
“I can dog-paddle a little.”

[P132]
“Get onto land before I beat you like a dog.”

[P133]
“Hmm. That would probably be better.”

[P134]
Gung Gibang stepped back, and Hyuk Mujin came forward.

[P135]
“Captain.”

[P136]
“You stay on land too. Keep your head down and hide. You won’t be any help if you charge in for no reason.”

[P137]
“I know. I only called out to encourage you.”

[P138]
“……”

[P139]
What a sibu-leol bastard. I felt what little strength I had left draining away.

[P140]
I let out a small sigh, then gave Cheongpung one final, earnest warning.

[P141]
“The Dongting Fisherman may or may not be in there. But if I find him and drag him outside…”

[P142]
Cheongpung nodded.

[P143]
“I won’t miss the opportunity.”

[P144]
“Good. That’s all I need.”

[P145]
I had no idea just how formidable the Dongting Fisherman was, but with Cheongpung’s help, things would be much easier.

[P146]
*Of course, he might not be here either.*

[P147]
But… how should I put it?

[P148]
This time felt different.

[P149]
It wasn’t reason. It was instinct.

[P150]
I looked at each of them in turn, then leaped without hesitation into the purple water.

[P151]
*Splash!*

[P152]
The familiar sensation washed over me as a System notification rang out.

[P153]
The Title’s effect activated. Transparent webbing formed between my fingers and toes, and breathing became easy.

[P154]
*Deeper. Farther in.*

[P155]
I pressed onward without stopping.

[P156]
I swam swiftly through the cold water, passing countless fish.

[P157]
Then I spotted something in the distance.

[P158]
*What’s that…?*

[P159]
Far ahead, a pitch-black cave came into view.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
